title: AgentSupply
description: Per-backend supply strategy and live status (spec §4.2, frames V6 01–04 / M01–M02). v3 keeps the spend order at the backend grain and adds the enabled named-Agent projection used to attribute model supply honestly.

mode.description: 中枢/直连. Existing users stay direct until they migrate; fresh installs default hub (plan §4). Under Option 1, hub mode for claude still consumes the subscription via the native channel per turn.

selected_by_agent.description: v2 (07-29, review round 4): the Vibe Agent whose `model` produced `selected_model_id`, by name — or null when the value came from the backend default (`agents.<backend>.default_model`) because that Agent pins no model. WHY THIS EXISTS: model selection does not live at the backend grain. Several enabled Vibe Agents can share one backend and each carry their own `model` (SQLite `agents.backend` + `agents.model`; on this machine today three enabled Agents share backend `claude` with three different models), and routing follows the selected Vibe Agent, not the backend (AGENTS.md → Agent routing model). The shipped projection already resolves ONE Agent — the global default, and only if its backend matches (`core/controller.py::default_vibe_agent_model`) — so this record has always answered for exactly one route while looking like it answered for the backend. Naming the Agent makes that scope readable instead of implied: a caller can see whose model it is, and knows it is not a claim about every turn on this backend. A per-Agent answer for any OTHER Agent is obtained the way every other model-scoped question already is — by passing that Agent's model explicitly to `GET /chain?model=` or `POST /probe {model}` (api.md → grain of the agent record). Derived, never persisted; null while mode=direct.

selected_model_id.description: v2 (07-29, review round 3): THE SELECTED MODEL of the route named by `selected_by_agent`, as the caller-facing MENU identifier — the built-in id for fixed menus, the prefixed vendor/model id for open menus. NOT a backend-wide fact (grain corrected 07-29, review round 4): it is the routed Vibe Agent's `model`, falling back to the backend default when that Agent pins none, and a different enabled Agent on the same backend can request a different model on its very next turn. Every projection below that depends on a model — `current`, `supply_status`, and the probe's default — therefore inherits that scope and answers for this route alone. Hoisted out of `current` in round 3, where round 2 had put it as `menu_model_id`. The bug was not merely that the selection was nested: `current` is null whenever nothing is runnable (`waiting` / `interrupted`), so the selection vanished from the payload in exactly the two states where the UI needs it most — 「当前无可用来源」 has to name the model it is talking about, the chain drill-in has to query one, and the probe has to default to one. A client would have had to remember the last non-null `current` and hope, or issue a second call. The two fields answer different questions and have different lifetimes: this one is a persisted user CHOICE that survives every supply state, while `current` is a momentary fact about the next turn. Nesting a choice inside a fact made the choice inherit the fact's nullability. null only when mode=direct (no hub selection exists). OPTIONAL here / required at the API boundary once the serializer emits it (README → required-vs-optional). Absent from this file's `examples` on purpose — they round-trip byte-faithfully through the shipped v1 serializer, which has no such field; the worked v2 payload including the `current: null` case lives in api.md.

selected_model_explicit.description: TRUE iff `selected_model_id` originates from the user's explicit configuration request; FALSE means no explicit model selection, including a resolver-picked value or no selected model.

current.description: What the next turn of THIS ROUTE would use (frame V6 01 supply row) — i.e. the first runnable candidate in this backend's chain for `selected_model_id`, which is the model of the Agent named by `selected_by_agent`. Inherits that grain: a different enabled Vibe Agent on the same backend requesting a different model has a different chain, and this field does not describe it (round 4). NULL IN THREE CASES, not one: (a) mode=direct; (b) `supply_status: "waiting"` — every candidate is cooling; (c) `supply_status: "interrupted"` — no candidate can recover unattended. In (b) and (c) the serializer MUST emit null rather than the last-used source: a stale `current` would render 使用中 for a source that will not be called, which is exactly the lie the taxonomy exists to prevent. Non-null ⇒ `supply_status` is ok or degraded. Carries only facts about that candidate — the selection itself is `selected_model_id`, one level up, because it outlives every one of these three nulls.

model_id.description: The RESOLVED upstream model id — what actually gets sent (e.g. `glm-5.2` or `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`). A property of this attempt, not of the selection, which is why it stays here while the selection moved out. NOT a valid input to the chain query or the probe: for open-menu backends the caller-facing identifier is prefixed (`zhipuai/glm-5.2`), while a fixed-menu native alias may be source-specific, so passing this value through would miss. Use the top-level `selected_model_id` for that. It equals `selected_model_id` only when neither an explicit mapping nor built-in native alias resolution changes the upstream id. Native alias resolution is automatic supply truth and does not create a mapping entry.

sources.description: This backend's source order — the ordered SUBSET of sources it spends, plus the policy that governs the order (spec §4.2). Replaces the removed global priority contract. Optional in this schema only because the frozen legacy examples predate it; it is REQUIRED at the API boundary. null while mode=direct.

policy.description: follow = 跟随推荐 (default): the server computes `order` from the recommendation rule and newly added eligible sources join automatically. THE RULE IS NOT RESTATED HERE. It lives in spec §4.2 under 'document verbatim, implement verbatim', with three ordered clauses plus the channel nuance (a native_cli and a consented hub-held subscription of the same own vendor share the first slot, native_cli first), the exhaustive-over-eligible-sources claim that makes auto-join safe, and the absent-`created_at` half-rule in source.schema.json. Round 2 tried to summarise it in one parenthesis and produced something both incomplete and misleading — it read as if only a native_cli subscription could hold the first slot, quietly excluding the hub-held case the spec explicitly admits. A determinism rule that two files describe differently is not deterministic, so this field points at the one home instead of keeping a second copy that can drift. custom = 自定义: a user-owned frozen subset; new sources do NOT join and the UI hints 「有新来源未启用」. Any manual edit while in follow forks the record to custom; 「恢复推荐顺序」 returns it to follow. The server never reorders a custom list (spec §2 promise 4).

order.description: Enabled source ids, position 0 = spend first. A SUBSET, not a permutation: sources this backend is ineligible for, or that the user removed, are absent. Authoritative — the server always re-echoes the full canonical order after any mutation; clients never compute partial reorders.

eligibility.description: v2: server-authoritative per-source inventory, one entry per existing source (spec §4.4). Eligibility makes the UI chokepoint isSourceEligible (ui/src/components/settings/models/menus/identifiers.ts, self-documented as ESCALATED) a pure projection instead of a second hand-written copy of the compatibility matrix. The channel class pass adds two request-grain signals to the SAME complete inventory: `in_current_model_chain` says whether this source supplies the selected route's current model, and `process_availability_reason` carries the serving process's native CLI readiness blocker. Keeping non-members with `in_current_model_chain: false` is load-bearing: embedding only AgentChain would omit an in-order source that does not supply the current model, taking the drawer's availability fact with it. REQUIRED AND NON-NULL whenever `sources` is an object (07-29, review round 5) — see the conditional at the bottom of this file. Mechanical API guards enforce one row per EXISTING source, every id in `order` present with `eligible: true`, and both new signal fields present on every row once the serializer lands them.

allOf.$comment: v2 (07-29, review round 4): `eligible: false` ⇒ a non-null key, and `eligible: true` ⇒ null, both as conditionals. This projection exists so the UI's isSourceEligible chokepoint stops being a second hand-written copy of the compatibility matrix — but an entry that says 不适用 without saying why hands the drawer a dead row: no explanation, and no way to pick between 「换个客户端」, 「OpenCode 只支持 API Key」 and 「需要先同意实验项」, which are three different remedies. The converse matters as much: a key on an eligible source would render an unavailability reason next to a source that is available.

reason_key.description: Closed i18n-key vocabulary explaining an ineligible source. REQUIRED and non-null when `eligible` is false, null when it is true. A new eligibility cause therefore requires an explicit contract and locale change.

in_current_model_chain.description: Membership in the CAPABILITY chain for this AgentSupply record's `selected_model_id`, at the same routed-Agent grain as `current`. true includes blocked members because availability does not change capability; false is the explicit not-supplying-current-model flag that keeps a source visible to the drawer; null exactly when `selected_model_id` is null. OPTIONAL here and REQUIRED at the API boundary with the serializer, so frozen v1 examples remain byte-faithful.

process_availability_reason.$comment: Owner-approved channel class pass, evidence at master 05f72ae5: core/handlers/model_hub/service.py:469-483 computes the per-backend unavailable native source set independently of source health, and service.py:1843-1891 already computes that set beside the complete eligibility inventory but emits neither fact. This bare token is the AgentSupply spelling of mirror row M8. It is legal only for a native_cli Source at the API assembly boundary; hub is definitionally process-available and therefore null.
process_availability_reason.description: Resolve-time serving-process availability for this source on this backend. `native_cli_unavailable` means this process cannot launch the sanctioned CLI under its own login right now; null means no process blocker. This does not restate source-global health. OPTIONAL here and REQUIRED at the API boundary with the serializer.

supply_status.$comment: Targeted v4 same-assumption audit (escalations #2+#3): this rollup is process-aware, not a health-only summary. Evidence at master 807d1eee: core/handlers/model_hub/service.py:1223-1229 supplies unavailable_source_ids to resolution; resolver.py:90-116 classifies waiting only when every blocked match is cooldown, not retry-ready, and not unavailable. Any unavailable member in a no-candidate chain therefore yields interrupted.
supply_status.description: Derived supply rollup (spec §4.5), computed per request and never persisted, for the model of the route named by `selected_by_agent`. It reads the same complete runnability predicate as AgentChain: source-global health permits AND this process can serve the channel. ok = serving from the intended head; degraded = serving through fallback and/or with blocked members; waiting = no runnable member and every member is a not-retry-ready cooldown that is process-available; interrupted = no runnable member and at least one blocker needs action — including a native CLI unavailable in this process at any health — or the capability chain is empty. null when mode=direct or when Hub has no pinned selection.

mappings.description: fixed-menu backends only; per-agent scope (spec §4.3 step 1). Absent entry = 跟随原生 (identity). A mapping chooses a MODEL, never a source.

builtin_id.description: real built-in model id, e.g. claude-opus-4-6

model_supply.description: v2: cheap per-menu-item chain summary so the 模型菜单 drawer can flag 「无来源可供」 without one chain query per row (spec §4.6). Read-only projection; the authoritative chain is GET /api/models/agents/<backend>/chain.

model_id.description: The identifier this backend's menu uses: the built-in id for fixed menus, the prefixed identifier (vendor/model) for open menus.

chain_length.$comment: Targeted v4 audit: capability visibility is not candidate availability. core/handlers/model_hub/resolver.py:252-273 at master 807d1eee builds matching_sources before source_runnable filters unavailable ids into candidates, so an unavailable native source remains counted and ordered in this projection.
chain_length.description: Length of the CAPABILITY chain — how many sources in this backend's order can supply this model at all, mapping applied — matching `AgentChain.chain`, including cooling and process-unavailable native CLI members. Deliberately NOT a count of currently-runnable candidates: this drives a menu row's 「无来源可供」 flag, which is structural and must not flicker with runtime state. 0 ⇒ flag the row; cooldown-only blocking appears as `supply_status: waiting`, while a native CLI unavailable in this process is `interrupted`.

named_agents.description: v3 read-only projection of every enabled named Vibe Agent on this backend. It is derived live from each Agent's pinned model, falling back to the backend default when the Agent inherits. The distinct name avoids collision with SupplyGap.agents, whose items are bare names inside a mutation-refusal payload.

effective_model_id.description: The Agent's pinned model, or the inherited backend default, in the caller-facing menu identifier namespace. null means no selection exists.

supply_status.description: This named Agent's own live rollup for effective_model_id. null in Direct mode or when effective_model_id is null.

builtin_models.description: v1.2 (2026-07-24 integration): fixed-menu backends only — real built-in model ids, server-populated from vibe/backend_model_catalog.py; null for open-menu backends. UI must not hardcode menus.

standard_vendors.description: v1.2 (2026-07-24 integration): opencode only — server-populated mirror of STANDARD_OPENCODE_VENDOR_IDS (core/handlers/model_hub/identifiers.py) so the UI never hand-mirrors vendor lists; null otherwise.

allOf.$comment: v2 (07-29, review round 4; completed in round 5): SWEEP of the fields that direct mode does not have, so the drawer can never render hub state for a backend writing its own settings.json. Round 4 swept the SENTENCE 'null when mode=direct' and caught five fields; round 5 found the sixth, `model_supply`, which states its hub-onlyness a different way ('per-menu-item CHAIN summary') and therefore escaped a grep-shaped sweep — the exact failure the round-4 note warned about one line later ('naming three of them would leave the fourth writable'). Lesson recorded rather than just patched: sweep by what a field MEANS, not by the phrasing it happens to use. `model_supply` is not merely redundant in direct mode, it is actively wrong: `chain_length` counts sources in this backend's `order`, and direct mode has no order, so every row would carry `chain_length: 0` and the menu would flag 「无来源可供」 on every model the native CLI supplies perfectly well. FOUR fields are deliberately NOT pinned by mode, recorded so the next reviewer can tell judgement from oversight: `mappings`, `menu`, `builtin_models` and `standard_vendors` are the user's MENU configuration, not hub runtime state. They survive a mode switch on purpose — a direct-mode Claude still has built-in models and still has whatever mapping table the user set up, which becomes active again the moment they migrate to hub. Zeroing them on `mode` would delete user configuration on a switch, contradicting the non-destructive copy-only migration promise (spec §5).

v3 Hub-mode half. `sources`, `model_supply`, and `named_agents` are non-null when present. Presence is deliberately enforced at the API boundary rather than here so the two frozen legacy examples, which predate these projections, remain valid. The selection fields are deliberately NOT constrained non-null: Hub with no explicit Vibe-Agent model and no backend default has no pinned selection. In that state each turn resolves the model carried by the request itself, so inventing a menu selection would be false state.
v3 D-1: a missing Hub selection is honest absence, never a projected builtin_models[0]. The route remains usable because a turn carries its own requested model.

v2 (07-29, review round 4): the two BLOCKED rollup values guarantee nothing is runnable, so `current` — 'what the next turn would use' — has nothing true to say and must be null. Round 3 documented this as three cases the serializer MUST honour and left all three writable; a stale `current` surviving into `waiting` renders 使用中 for a source that will not be called, which is the single lie the whole taxonomy was built to prevent (spec §4.5: `current` is null in both states, so neither ever renders a stale 使用中).

v2 (07-29, review round 4): and the converse the field already claimed ('Non-null ⇒ supply_status is ok or degraded'), plus the mode half. A record that names a serving source while reporting a blocked rollup is contradictory in the other direction, and either half alone leaves that payload writable. PRESENCE DELIBERATELY NOT REQUIRED here (07-29, review round 5), the one declared exception to the rule that a non-null `then` constraint must also require its field: this file's frozen examples carry `current` with no `supply_status` at all — they round-trip byte-faithfully through the SHIPPED v1 serializer, which has no such field — so `required: ["supply_status"]` would fail the contract gate rather than strengthen it. The obligation moves to the API boundary, where the v2 serializer emits it (README → required-vs-optional). Absence is also the fail-safe direction: no rollup means no claim about health and no action-required claim, whereas the dangerous absences (`severity` on a needs_action event, `current` under an ok rollup) are all required above. The exception is enforced as a declared entry in the round-5 presence checker, so 'missing on purpose' cannot decay into 'missing by accident' (api.md → Serializer completeness).

v2 (07-29, review round 5): the RUNNABLE half of the rollup ⇒ `current`, which round 4 left open at both ends. It pinned 'blocked ⇒ current null' and 'current non-null ⇒ not blocked', and those two together still admit `supply_status: "ok"` with `current: null` — a record claiming 正在从链首供给 while refusing to name the source doing it. That is not a hypothetical shape: it is what a serializer produces the moment the rollup and the candidate are computed by different code paths and one of them returns early, and the drawer would render 使用中 with an empty source row. `ok` and `degraded` are DEFINED by something being served (§4.5: serving from the head of the chain / serving via a fallback), so the candidate exists by construction and the payload must carry it. `required` is part of the fix, not decoration: draft-07 `properties` only validates fields that are PRESENT, so a `then` naming `current` without requiring it passes any record that just omits the key — which is how the whole class of round-4 conditionals ended up weaker than it read. With this member the pair `supply_status` × `current` is total: each of the four rollup values determines whether a candidate is named, in both directions.

v2 (07-29, review round 4): menu shape ⇒ which menu fields exist. `menu` is open-menu only, `mappings` and `builtin_models` are fixed-menu only, `standard_vendors` is opencode only — four prose-only scopings, all four writable until now. These are the fields the UI branches on to decide whether to render a checkbox list or a mapping table, so a record carrying both leaves that choice to whichever field the component happens to read first.

v2 (07-29, review round 4): menu shape is a property of the BACKEND, not a free choice — spec §4.2 names them one by one (open menus i.e. OpenCode; fixed menus i.e. Claude Code and Codex). Pinned so the pairing cannot drift per payload; a new backend joining the enum is a contract change that comes here to declare which kind it is.

v2 (07-29, review round 5): a `sources` object ⇒ a real `eligibility` array. `eligibility` sat optional AND nullable inside a container that only a v2 serializer can emit, which made the field's own reason for existing waivable: it exists so the UI chokepoint `isSourceEligible` becomes a pure projection instead of a second hand-written copy of the compatibility matrix, and a null there sends the drawer straight back to computing the matrix itself — the duplicate this contract was written to delete, restored by omission. Nothing blocks the server from computing it: `sources` being non-null already means hub mode with a resolved order, and eligibility is a pure function of the source set and this backend (spec §4.4). Note the nesting is what makes this safe — the top-level `sources` stays optional for the byte-faithful v1 round-trip, so this fires only on records that already carry v2 shape. INVARIANT NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE, and named rather than dropped: every id in `order` MUST appear in `eligibility` with `eligible: true` — you cannot spend a source this backend is not eligible for, and 'one entry per existing source' makes the coverage half a definition, not a preference. Draft-07 cannot compare one array's items against another's without `$data`, so the guard is mechanical instead of schematic (api.md → Serializer completeness). Stating it here so the next reviewer reads a known limit rather than an oversight.
